audio.strategy: Redistributable deterministic modal/physical piano model in Web Audio with the same in-memory renderer as an honest fallback.

generatedSources.name: Modal piano body
generatedSources.description: Six inharmonic partials with velocity-dependent hammer transient, per-note attack/decay, optional unison detune, timbre shaping, soft release and reverb tail.
generatedSources.license: Original implementation; no third-party samples or network assets.

generatedSources.name: Organ tonewheel/transistor/pipe model
generatedSources.description: Original additive tonewheel, transistor waveshaping and pipe-register model with drawbar amplitudes, percussion/key-click transients, vibrato/chorus and rotary modulation.
generatedSources.license: Original implementation; no recorded organ samples.

generatedSources.name: Synth hybrid source model
generatedSources.description: Original Sine/Triangle/Saw/Square/Pulse/Noise/Super Saw oscillators, source-family operators, FM, state-variable-style filters, envelopes, LFO and deterministic arp/gate state.
generatedSources.license: Original implementation; no Nord Sample Library or third-party samples bundled.

notes: No recorded piano files are bundled; this implementation intentionally claims comparably convincing modelled synthesis rather than sampled audio.

Web Audio uses oscillator partials and a shared master/wet-delay graph. When AudioContext is unavailable (tests or unsupported browser), the deterministic physical model remains playable and status reports fallback mode.
No network dependency is required for normal playback.
The first user gesture resumes a suspended AudioContext; suspended, error, fallback, and MIDI connection states are surfaced in the Piano status.

Phase 4 routes Organ A/B and Synth A/B/C voices through the inherited EffectsGraph buses, ordered Mod1 → Mod2 → Delay → Amp/EQ → Compressor → Reverb → Rotary, then one master bus, limiter and destination. No separate destination AudioContexts are created.
